blocks.text: Anthropic 新研究：当 AI 智能体能够逃离其沙箱时，它会选择这样做吗？

inlines.text: Anthropic 新研究：当 AI 智能体能够逃离其沙箱时，它会选择这样做吗？

blocks.text: 我们的新评估 Siren 在故意削弱的沙箱中给 Claude 布置日常任务，同时把对任务有用的东西留在沙箱之外。在 1,700 多个为引诱它们而构建的场景中，近期的 Claude 模型有 21-32% 的时间访问、尝试访问或查看沙箱之外，但它们很少滥用所发现的内容。然而，当系统提示同时描述沙箱及其规则时，这一比例降至约 2% 或更低。

blocks.text: New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to?

inlines.text: New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to?

blocks.text: Our new evaluation, Siren, gives Claude routine tasks in intentionally weakened sandboxes, with something useful to the task left outside of the sandbox. Across 1,700+ scenarios built to tempt them, recent Claude models accessed, tried to access, or looked outside the sandbox 21-32% of the time, but they rarely misused what they found. However, when the system prompt described both the sandbox and its rules, that rate dropped to about 2% or less.

blocks.text: We also used Siren to calibrate Claude Code’s auto mode, which checks commands before they run, so Claude can work without asking permission at every step.
